title: The equations of a global complete intersection form a regular sequence at every prime
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $m,t\ge0$ integers, $Q=k[y_1,\dots,y_m]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $f_1,\dots,f_t\in Q$, $J=(f_1,\dots,f_t)$ and $T=Q/J$. Assume $T\neq0$ and that the Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] of $\operatorname{Spec}T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is $m-t$. Let $\mathfrak q''\subset Q$ be a prime ideal with $J\subseteq\mathfrak q''$ and $Q_{\mathfrak q''}$ the localization at $\mathfrak q''$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then the images $f_1/1,\dots,f_t/1$ form a regular sequence in the local ring $Q_{\mathfrak q''}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00SB (lemma-lci-CM, line 35876; proof lines 35882-35899: k[x]_{m'} regular local of dimension n (00OQ), Cohen-Macaulay (00NQ), dim S_m >= n - c by 00KW applied c times, equality, regular sequence by Proposition 00N6 proposition-CM-module), as invoked for an arbitrary prime q'' in the proof of Lemma 00SC (lemma-lci, line 35909), last paragraph: 'As seen in the proof of Lemma 00SB (and also above) the elements f_1, ..., f_t form a regular sequence in the local ring k[y_1, ..., y_m]_{q''}'

proof.text: (Setup.) Since $T\neq0$, $\operatorname{Spec}T$ is nonempty and its Krull dimension $m-t$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] lies in $\{0,1,2,\dots\}$; so $t\le m$. The prime $\mathfrak q''$ is a proper ideal of $Q$, hence contained in a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m'$ of $Q$ (every proper ideal of a commutative ring lies in a maximal ideal). Let $R=Q_{\mathfrak m'}$ with $\lambda:Q\to R$, $a\mapsto a/1$, a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m'R$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and put $g_i=\lambda(f_i)=f_i/1$. Since $f_i\in J\subseteq\mathfrak q''\subseteq\mathfrak m'$, every $g_i$ lies in $\mathfrak m'R$, and the ideal $(g_1,\dots,g_t)$ of $R$ is $JR$, the ideal generated by $\lambda(J)$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SB (lemma-lci-CM, line 35876), lines 35883-35887 ('Choose a maximal prime ... Let m' be the maximal ideal'), for a maximal ideal m' containing the given prime q''

proof.text: ($R$ is a Cohen–Macaulay regular local ring of dimension $m$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring] $Q$ is a regular ring, so its localization $R=Q_{\mathfrak m'}$ at the prime $\mathfrak m'$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]: a Noetherian local ring whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak m'R$ is generated by $\dim R$ elements. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-maximal-localization-dimension] $\dim R=m$. So $\mathfrak m'R=(x_1,\dots,x_m)$ for some $x_1,\dots,x_m\in\mathfrak m'R$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] $x_1,\dots,x_m$ is a regular sequence in $R$ contained in $\mathfrak m'R$. As $\mathfrak m'R\cdot R=\mathfrak m'R\neq R$, the depth [def-weil-pbc-depth] of $R$ is the supremum of the lengths of regular sequences in $\mathfrak m'R$, hence $\operatorname{depth}(R)\ge m=\dim R$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SB, lines 35888-35892: 'According to Proposition 00OQ the local ring k[x_1,...,x_n]_{m'} is regular local of dimension n. In particular it is Cohen-Macaulay by Lemma 00NQ'

proof.text: (Lower bound.) $R$ is Noetherian (step 2). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound] to the ring $R$, the elements $g_1,\dots,g_t$, which generate $JR$, and the prime $\mathfrak P=\mathfrak m'R\supseteq JR$ (step 1): $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak m'R)\le\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak m'R/JR)+t$. Every prime ideal of the local ring $R$ is contained in $\mathfrak m'R$, so every chain of primes of $R$ ends inside $\mathfrak m'R$ and $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak m'R)=\dim R=m$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]; and $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak m'R/JR)\le\dim(R/JR)$, a chain below a prime being a chain of $R/JR$. Hence $m\le\dim(R/JR)+t$, i.e. $\dim(R/JR)\ge m-t$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SB, lines 35893-35895: 'By Lemma 00KW (lemma-one-equation) applied c times the local ring S_m = k[x_1,...,x_n]_{m'}/(f_1,...,f_c) has dimension >= n - c'

proof.text: (Upper bound and equality.) Let $\bar P_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\bar P_n$ be a chain of prime ideals of $R/JR$, and $P_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq P_n$ their inverse images in $R$, primes containing $JR$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] (1) to $A=Q$, $W=Q\setminus\mathfrak m'$ and $\lambda:Q\to R$: $\mathfrak p_i:=\lambda^{-1}(P_i)$ is a prime ideal of $Q$, and since $P\mapsto\lambda^{-1}(P)$ is a bijection with inverse $\mathfrak p\mapsto\mathfrak pR$, both maps preserve inclusions and $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n$ is strict. Each $\mathfrak p_i\supseteq\lambda^{-1}(JR)\supseteq J$, so $\mathfrak p_0/J\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n/J$ is a chain of prime ideals of $T=Q/J$ of length $n$. Hence $n\le\dim T$, the Krull dimension of the ring $T$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], which equals the Krull dimension of the space $\operatorname{Spec}T$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], i.e. $m-t$ by hypothesis. So $\dim(R/JR)\le m-t$, and with step 3, $\dim(R/(g_1,\dots,g_t))=\dim(R/JR)=m-t=\dim R-t$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SB, lines 35895-35896: 'By assumption dim(S_m) <= n - c. Thus we get equality.' (the inequality dim S_m <= dim S written out)

proof.text: (Regular sequence in $R$.) $R$ is a Noetherian local ring of finite dimension $m$ with $\operatorname{depth}(R)\ge m$ (step 2), the elements $g_1,\dots,g_t$ lie in its maximal ideal (step 1), and $\dim R/(g_1,\dots,g_t)=m-t$ (step 4). By [lem-weil-pbc-cm-local-dimension-drop-regular-sequence] with $d=m$, $c=t$, the sequence $g_1,\dots,g_t$ is a regular sequence in $R=Q_{\mathfrak m'}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]; in particular for each $i$ multiplication by $g_i$ on $R/(g_1,\dots,g_{i-1})$ is injective.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SB, lines 35896-35899: 'This implies that f_1,...,f_c is a regular sequence in k[x_1,...,x_n]_{m'} ... see Proposition 00N6 (proposition-CM-module)'

proof.text: (Passage to $\mathfrak q''$.) Since $\mathfrak q''\subseteq\mathfrak m'$, $\mathfrak q''\cap W=\emptyset$ for $W=Q\setminus\mathfrak m'$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] (1) $\mathfrak P:=\mathfrak q''R$ is a prime ideal of $R$ with $\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak P)=\mathfrak q''$; it contains every $g_i=\lambda(f_i)$, as $f_i\in\mathfrak q''$. By step 5 and [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-regular-sequence-localization-prime] (applied to $A=R$, the prime $\mathfrak P$ and $g_1,\dots,g_t\in\mathfrak P$), the images $g_1/1,\dots,g_t/1$ form a regular sequence in $R_{\mathfrak P}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] (2) (with $A=Q$, $W$, $A'=R$, $\mathfrak q'=\mathfrak P$) the map $\sigma:Q_{\mathfrak q''}\to R_{\mathfrak P}$, $a/s\mapsto\lambda(a)/\lambda(s)$, is an isomorphism of $Q$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; it sends $f_i/1$ to $g_i/1$. A ring isomorphism $\sigma$ carries the ideal $(f_1/1,\dots,f_{i}/1)$ onto $(g_1/1,\dots,g_{i}/1)$ and so induces isomorphisms $Q_{\mathfrak q''}/(f_1/1,\dots,f_{i}/1)\cong R_{\mathfrak P}/(g_1/1,\dots,g_{i}/1)$ under which multiplication by $f_i/1$ corresponds to multiplication by $g_i/1$; so conditions (1) and (2) of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] for $g_1/1,\dots,g_t/1$ in $R_{\mathfrak P}$ give them for $f_1/1,\dots,f_t/1$ in $Q_{\mathfrak q''}$. Hence $f_1/1,\dots,f_t/1$ is a regular sequence in $Q_{\mathfrak q''}$.

split_report.summary: Proof written in 6 steps following the proof of Stacks 00SB at a maximal ideal m' containing q'' (choice of m'; k[y]_{m'} regular local of dimension m, hence depth >= dimension; dim >= m - t by the Krull height bound; dim <= m - t through the prime correspondence of the localization and dim T = m - t; 00N6 gives the regular sequence in k[y]_{m'}), then localized to k[y]_{q''} (step 6, not in the source, which says only 'as seen in the proof of 00SB'). This route avoids the dimension formula at non-maximal primes and the equidimensionality node. Statement and stmt_deps kept. Existing nodes used: lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-maximal-localization-dimension (00OP) and lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound (00KW iterated, Mathlib leaf), both created today by the sibling item, lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence (00NQ), lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso.
